text: dsh-subscription-logins 为 DSH Web 增加 Logins 设置页，通过 host 与浏览器远程接口连接授权服务。用户可为 OpenAI Codex、Anthropic 和 Z.AI 保存多个命名登录，完成授权后切换、重命名或删除账号，并自动补充模型提供方设置。适合在 DSH Web 管理多组模型订阅凭据的用户；Z.AI 登录需 API key。

dsh-subscription-logins adds a Logins page to DSH Web Settings for managing OpenAI Codex, Anthropic, and Z.AI accounts. Users can authorize named logins, switch accounts, rename or remove them, and add matching model provider settings. Z.AI requires an API key.
想在 DSH Web 的设置里保存并切换多个模型订阅账号
怎样用不同的 ChatGPT、Claude 或 Z.AI 登录来使用 DSH 模型？
I want to manage and switch between saved model provider logins in DSH Web.
dsh-subscription-logins 的功能「提供方登录」：在 Logins 页面为 OpenAI Codex、Anthropic 或 Z.AI 新增登录，并查看授权状态或提示。
dsh-subscription-logins 的功能「保存账号切换」：登录凭据按账号归档，用户可在页面选择当前账号、修改名称或移除账号；选中账号会同步到对应模型提供方凭据记录。
dsh-subscription-logins 将凭据保存在 DSH credential store；Z.AI 登录要求 API key。

dsh-subscription-logins README · dsh-subscription-logins：Manage subscription credentials for DSH's `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, and `zai` providers. The plugin adds a short **Logins** entry beside Models in Settings and drives the provider flows supplied by pi-ai.

dsh-subscription-logins README · dsh-subscription-logins：This is a pure bundle plugin. It does not patch DeepSeek Harness. Its composition layer mounts the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-authorization` service, which causes the existing `llm-pi-ai` plugin to register its provider login flows. The plugin's host half exposes only the `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, and `zai` flows to its own browser half through a Typert Remote.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/deepseek-harness/plugins/subscription-logins
```

Restart `dsh web`, then open **Settings → Logins**. Name each login as you add it, for example `Work` or `Personal`. The page keeps multiple credentials per provider and marks one active. Select **Use** to change the account used by the next model request.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：- For ChatGPT, select **Sign in with ChatGPT**, open the verification page, and enter the displayed code if OpenAI uses the device-code path.
- For Claude, select **Sign in with Claude**, finish the browser flow, and paste the callback URL or authorization code if requested.
- For Z.AI, create an API key after subscribing to the GLM Coding Plan, then enter it in the masked prompt. Z.AI uses API keys rather than browser OAuth.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：The `zai` route uses pi-ai's dedicated Coding Plan endpoint, `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`. Z.AI says Coding Plan benefits are limited to supported tools and products. Confirm that DSH usage complies with the current [GLM Coding Plan usage policy](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/usage-policy) before relying on subscription quota. See Z.AI's [Coding Plan quick start](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/quick-start) for API key setup.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：The Claude option exposes pi-ai's existing Anthropic OAuth flow, but it does not promise that requests will be included in a Claude Pro or Max subscription. Anthropic's published login policy says third-party tools should normally use API keys. It may restrict OAuth access or charge usage credits. See [Anthropic's account login policy](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13189465-log-in-to-your-claude-account).

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：OpenAI currently labels device-code authentication as beta. If it is unavailable, enable device-code login in your personal ChatGPT security settings or ask your workspace admin to allow it. A normal browser callback flow may be offered instead.

After login, the plugin adds the matching `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, or `zai` provider to **Settings → Models** with an empty native profile. Existing provider settings are never replaced. Choose one of that provider's models for a session.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：The adapter still reads its canonical `llm-pi-ai/<provider>` record. The plugin archives named credentials under its own credential scope and copies the selected credential into that canonical record. Before switching, it saves the current canonical record back to the active archive so token refreshes survive account changes. An existing canonical credential is imported as `Existing login` and can be renamed.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Install：Removing a saved login deletes its archived credential. Removing the active login also deletes the provider's canonical record. These records contain sensitive access tokens, refresh tokens, and API keys. Protect the DSH home directory, and never commit or share its credential files.

dsh-subscription-logins README · Why this is a separate Settings page：The public client extension API has a `settings.section` slot, but the built-in Models page does not declare a slot inside provider cards. Registering a neighboring page uses the supported plugin API and survives client rebuilds. Modifying `ProviderEditor` or the host API proxy would put part of the feature back into harness core.
section: Why this is a separate Settings page
